title: Learning Shortest Paths with Generative Flow Networks
venue: ICML 2026 SPIGM Workshop (unverified: arXiv comment empty, no header in PDF; label inherited from prior survey)
one_line_en: Minimizing the expected trajectory length of a non-acyclic GFlowNet is equivalent to assigning zero probability to every non-shortest trajectory (Theorem 3.4, iff), which reduces unweighted shortest-path search to training a flow-regularized non-acyclic GFlowNet whose backward policy solves the task.
one_line_zh: 非无环 GFlowNet 的期望轨迹长度取最小值，当且仅当所有非最短路轨迹被赋零概率（定理 3.4，充要）；据此把任意无权图的最短路问题归约为训练一个带流正则的非无环 GFlowNet，训完的后向策略即最短路求解器，在魔方上以更小 beam 预算达到 SOTA 可比解长。
key_results: Lemma 3.2: E[n_tau] >= sum_x P_B(x | s_f) l(x) via the tower property plus l(x) as a per-trajectory floor
Lemma 3.3: a constructive parent map par(s) with l(s) = l(par(s)) + 1 attains E[n_tau] = sum_x R(x)/Z * l(x)
Theorem 3.4: minimizing E[n_tau] is equivalent (iff) to zero probability on all non-shortest trajectories; optimal P_B is generally not unique (Remark 3.5)
Assumption 3.1 replaces T36's P_B > 0 by E[n_tau] < infinity, since the optimal policy must zero out non-shortest edges (Appendix A)
Section 3.2 reduction: reverse the edges, set s0 = v_g, make every vertex terminal, take R = 1; then optimal E[n_tau] equals the average shortest-path length
Table 1 2x2x2 cube: optimal average 10.64 reached at W = 2^6 versus W = 2^10 for CayleyPy Cube (16x smaller beam), full solve rate even at W = 1
Table 1 3x3x3 cube: better at small beams (W = 2^9: 23.49 vs 24.34), comparable at large beams (W = 2^18: 21.24 vs 21.15)
Runtime at W = 2^18 on one NVIDIA H200: 1.74 s per configuration (25M params) versus 6.19 s for CayleyPy Cube (4M params), attributed to one forward pass emitting logits for all neighbours
assumptions: finite directed graph with Assumption 2.1 (s0 no incoming edges, s_f no outgoing edges, every state reachable from s0 and reaching s_f)
Assumption 3.1: backward random walk from s_f has finite expected length E[n_tau] < infinity
R > 0 on all terminal states; the reduction uses R = 1
every vertex of the input graph can reach the goal vertex v_g
theory characterizes exact minimizers; training uses the soft lambda penalty and beam search absorbs the approximation gap
bridge_to_O08: single-source (s0) shortest path with cost l(x) = d(s0, x); O08 adds F(s0->u) = L(u) to lift it to multi-source Kantorovich OT with cost d(u,x). Lemma 3.2 corresponds to O08 Eq. (18); Lemma 3.3 corresponds to O08 Theorem 3.2 Part 1; O08 Theorem 3.3 re-derives this claim through LP duality.
not_in_paper: numeric table for the Swap Puzzle (only Figure 2 curves)
comparison against classical BFS / bidirectional BFS on medium graphs
analysis of the N_max truncation's effect on the optimum
explanation of why the best lambda differs by five orders of magnitude between the 2x2x2 and 3x3x3 cubes
weighted or cost-sensitive graphs (listed as future work in Section 5)
